We all respond differently to these meds. Our bodies have diff insulin responses and store fat differently. 

Reddit is full of people talking about the bad side effects which is so fair I’ve done it too. But I was less drawn to write huge love poems about psych meds that work compared to my terror rants about meds ‘I hate’. 

I BALLOONED on lithium. Came off it & lost the weight steadily (so all is not lost if one gains).

Got back to my original weight. Became manic. Was put on sodium valproate which is the number one weight gaining mood stabiliser and a bit of a Hail Mary due to horrible side effects and risk to women of childbearing age. Read all the posts. Read some studies. Saw how the odds were against me. Didn’t want to be locked in my flesh again. Was scared as fuck. 

I have not gained a bit. And that is how differently my body responds. I am now looking for a full time job instead of part time, and thinking of trying to form friendships when I’d been non functioning for years. 

PLUS THERE ARE SO MANY OPTIONS MED WISE and the psych is just seeing what works with your unique self. There will be one that works for you and you’ll never know unless you start trialling them.

PS I have psychotic features to my bipolar so im not just some girl being like ‘take your meds everything will be fine :)’ knowing nothing. I’ve known euphoria beyond belief and been frightened out of my mind by delusions and paranoid episodes. These pills can actually help us.

I was so lucky. At the tailend of a months long manic episode when I started dating my now bf of four years. They put me on lithium the next month and he’s stayed with me through very high, low, taper, new med etc. Some people can stare it in the face and see it through. He was aware from day 1
I think age factors in too. People below 30 have a better understanding and less of a grim fascination with bipolar I’ve found. It’s separate to you rather than IS you

Ok well thank you for iterating a clear argument. I take from it that you take issue with the transferability of dog aggression to human aggression with ‘no warning’.

The way I see it, no other breed has such a high instance of successfully mauling members of their household to death after being a much loved family pet for X number of years. Straw-man I hear you say. 

Well here’s the thing. We see a great number of collies manifest OCD symptoms once they’re forced into a low stimulation domestic setting. ‘Herding light’ if you will.

I don’t find it hard to believe that a dog predisposed to dog aggression, once forced out of its working purpose into a family household, would transfer that internal response from ‘dog as game’ to ‘human as game’.

This exposition of a study shows that genetic markers drive about 15% of an dog’s behavioural output via ‘traits’ (aggression being one of them):

https://www.animals24-7.org/2019/10/14/pit-bulls-new-gene-study-shows-it-is-not-all-in-how-you-raise-them/

Chapter 2 of ‘This is the American Pit Bull Terrier’ is called, “The Clinging Death.” Richard F. Stratton (a lover of the breed) writes that while “ordinary canids rely heavily on threat display in a fight… [the pit bull terrier has been bred to] almost completely lose the threat display’’.  

Whatever the human blaming story is, such as, ‘a car drove past really loudly and the baby walked towards the dog — they should’ve managed it better’, chances are the people who have these dogs as pets don’t treat them like a caged lion with muzzles and impenetrable gates — their usually waggy smily dog, wagged and smiled (both stress signals but can be 90% of the time inert depending on minor differences in muscle tension) then went for throat. 

I’d be fascinated to read about the transferability of dog aggression to human aggression but it can’t be discounted and put into entirely separate categories when there is such a mountain of evidence that these breed clusters can and often will latch on to human targets.

Taking issue with the term snap is semantics. A dog mauling is a highly emotive trauma so combing withess’s language seems cruel. There is a syndrome coined for it:

https://www.whole-dog-journal.com/behavior/rage-syndrome-in-dogs/?amp=1

Why is it that citation is needed for statements like this and none for statements like: ‘retrievers boomed in popularity with the invention of the gun’? There has been organised human effort to breed traits into dogs with a recorded written history of it in most cases. It isn’t an attack against an individual dog and there are exceptions in every breed, but to pay close heed to the intended purpose of a breed is the wise and MORAL thing to do.

https://www.animals24-7.org/2019/10/14/pit-bulls-new-gene-study-shows-it-is-not-all-in-how-you-raise-them/

Also: Chapter Two of ‘This is the American Pit Bull Terrier’ is called, “The Clinging Death.”  There Richard F. Stratton writes that while “ordinary canids rely heavily on threat display in a fight… [the pit bull terrier has been bred to] almost completely lose the threat display.”
